notes: Live Shopify storefront (b7e869-b6.myshopify.com), direct HTTP fetch (collections.json, products.json, homepage HTML) worked throughout, no blocking. Enumerated all 155 collections via /en-intl/collections.json and cross-checked against the site's own mega-menu (fetched /en-intl homepage HTML): found three genuine, separately-merchandised Bestsellers listings, one per top-level shop section (Wallpaper, Fabric, Home Decor), each linked from that section's own nav-drop menu with aria-label/link text 'Bestsellers'. No unified /collections/bestsellers parent page exists (not in collections.json, not in nav) so these are emitted as three sibling rows, not group+children. Furniture's nav-drop menu has no Bestsellers link (only 'New In', 'Bespoke', 'Free Interior Design Services') so no Furniture Bestsellers PLP exists. QTY: collections.json products_count (35/35/36) proved inflated by 1 for Fabric and Home Decor, exactly as flagged project-wide in the prior Home-Decor pass notes for this company - qty instead taken from live /collections/<handle>/products.json?limit=250, counted by unique product id, page=2 confirmed empty for exhaustion on all three, and each page=1 fetch independently re-fetched a second time producing an identical id set (no session drift): Wallpaper 35, Fabric 34, Home Decor 35. Site's own search (/en-intl/search?q=...&type=product) returned a static 'No results' string for every query tried including 'bestsellers' itself (a term with 3 confirmed real listings) - proof the search results page is client-rendered/non-discriminating here, so navigation + collections.json enumeration was used as the reliable evidence source instead, per the zero-result-is-not-proof-of-absence rule.
